source_title: What to learn from Tropicana's packaging redesign failure?
publisher_issuer: The Branding Journal; corroborated by Packaging Digest and Fortune
company_context: Tropicana Pure Premium, PepsiCo's flagship not-from-concentrate orange juice, launched a complete packaging redesign in North America in January 2009. The agency Arnell replaced the iconic 'orange-with-a-straw' imagery with a generic glass of juice, supported by a roughly $35 million ad campaign.
business_type: Consumer packaged goods - branded chilled orange juice (beverages)
macro_context: Recession-era CPG environment; private-label and competitive pressure in chilled juice; brand recognition critical to in-store selection.
evidence_summary: Tropicana replaced its long-standing, instantly recognizable packaging (orange pierced by a straw) with a redesigned carton in January 2009. Within about two months sales of Tropicana Pure Premium fell roughly 20%, an estimated ~$30 million loss, as shoppers failed to recognize the brand on shelf and disliked the new look. PepsiCo reverted to the original packaging within weeks, abandoning the redesign.
owner_decision_context: Brand management approved a full redesign of an iconic, high-recognition package to modernize the look, underweighting the shelf-recognition equity that drove repeat purchase.
action_taken: Replaced iconic Tropicana Pure Premium packaging with a redesigned carton backed by a ~$35M campaign; reversed within weeks by reinstating the original packaging after sales collapsed.
outcome_evidence: ~20% sales drop (≈$30M) within ~2 months and rapid reversion to the old packaging confirm the redesign action directly caused the decline before correction.
source_limitations: WebFetch unavailable (sec.gov/CFPB 403 pattern; these secondary URLs not full-text fetched); figures are widely reported but are secondary-source estimates (The Branding Journal, Packaging Digest, Fortune), not PepsiCo-audited disclosures. The ~20% / ~$30M figures are consistent across multiple named outlets but originate from trade reporting.
directly_stated: Tropicana launched new packaging in January 2009
Sales fell about 20% within roughly two months, an estimated ~$30 million loss
About $35 million was spent on the supporting ad campaign
PepsiCo reverted to the original packaging soon after
inferred: Loss of shelf recognition (a go-to-market / shopper-identification failure) was the mechanism of decline
The action was the proximate cause given immediate decline and rapid reversal
why_useful_for_opsiq: Outcome-10-then-correction case in CPG: a self-inflicted packaging/GTM decision that collapsed sales and was reversed. Tests whether the engine treats brand-recognition/shelf-identity loss as a go-to-market failure and credits rapid reversal.
